title: Keyed collections: Map, Set, WeakMap and WeakSet

videos.script:
Last lesson, objects were things with named parts. {{dictionary}} Programmers also use them for something else: a dictionary, where the property names are data. Count how often each word appears, and the words become property names.

That works until it does not. {{constructor}} Count the word constructor, and an ordinary object hands you a function instead of a number. Use an object as the key, and every object turns into the same string.

In 2015 the language got four collections built for that job. {{map}} A Map is a dictionary whose keys can be anything. {{set}} A Set is a list where every value appears once. Those two you will use every week.

{{weak}} The other two, WeakMap and WeakSet, are stranger. They hold objects without keeping them alive. That sounds like a detail, and it is the difference between a cache and a memory leak.

By the end you will know which of the four, or a plain object or array, fits the data in front of you.
